report.summary: Partial findings only. The Prometheus target m0-otel-20260909 returned just two metric names, traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket (discovery for kube_.*, app_.*, http_.*, rpc_.* patterns returned those same two names and no kube-state, rpc or http series). On traces_span_metrics_calls_total the recorded service_name values are frontend, checkout and payment. For checkout the only status_code values are STATUS_CODE_ERROR and STATUS_CODE_UNSET (no OK value; UNSET means no status tag, not success), and spans with STATUS_CODE_ERROR are present at every evaluated point of the 24h window: at 1h steps the checkout ERROR series held 6,8,10,12,14 repeating while UNSET held 30,31,32,33,34 repeating, and the identical pattern and values appear at the start (2026-11-15T23:14) and end (2026-11-16T22:14) of the window. So checkout's own error reading is non-zero, but no onset or deviation can be located inside the authorized window, and no baseline outside it exists. A payment STATUS_CODE_ERROR series (9,12,15,18,21 repeating) is present in the same response; payment returned no UNSET series. Important data-quality counter-evidence: the same values came back for 5m, 10m and 1h range widths and for a raw non-rate query, queries filtered to service_name="checkout" and to service_name="payment" both returned the full checkout+payment series set, and a query for rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count and for duration buckets returned status_code-labelled series identical to calls_total — the metrics backend did not discriminate by expression, label or filter, so operation-level, RPC-level and dependency-level attribution cannot be derived from it. Jaeger was unavailable: all four traces_search attempts returned status error with reason SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span, operation name, error detail or parent-child edge was observed. span_name label values for checkout returned no_data. No Kubernetes state exists in this target, so no Deployment/Pod can be named. Hypotheses that remain open: payment as the origin of checkout's errors (correlation only, no trace edge), and an operation-specific or configuration/rollout cause (untestable with the available sources). No root-cause object can be identified, so root_cause is null.

claims.text: Only two metric names were discoverable in the authorized Prometheus target: traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket. A discovery for {__name__=~"kube_.*"} and one for {__name__=~"app_.*|http_.*|rpc_.*"} both returned exactly those two trace metric names, so no kube-state, app transaction, http_server or rpc_client series were returned.
The service_name label values present on traces_span_metrics_calls_total are frontend, checkout and payment.

For service_name="checkout" the only status_code label values returned are STATUS_CODE_ERROR and STATUS_CODE_UNSET; no OK/STATUS_CODE_OK value was returned, and STATUS_CODE_UNSET denotes spans carrying no status tag rather than success.

At 1h steps over the whole authorized window, checkout's STATUS_CODE_ERROR series repeated the cycle 6,8,10,12,14 and its STATUS_CODE_UNSET series repeated 30,31,32,33,34, from the first evaluated point (2026-11-15T23:14:08) to the last (2026-11-16T22:14:08); a raw (non-rate) query of the same metric returned the same per-timestamp values. Checkout therefore has a persistent non-zero error-status span count, with no segment of the window distinguishable from the others.
A payment STATUS_CODE_ERROR series is present in the same responses, repeating 9,12,15,18,21 per evaluated point; no payment STATUS_CODE_UNSET series was returned.

The metric responses did not vary with the expression, label or filter applied: increase[5m], increase[10m] and increase[1h] of traces_span_metrics_calls_total returned the same per-timestamp values (a non-counter-like pattern), a query filtered to service_name="checkout" and one filtered to service_name="payment" both returned the identical checkout(UNSET,ERROR)+payment(ERROR) series set, and queries for rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count and for traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket returned the same status_code-labelled series as calls_total instead of the rpc_grpc_status_code or le labels requested. This blocks any operation-level, RPC-level or dependency-level attribution from these metrics.

frontend is listed as a service_name value on traces_span_metrics_calls_total, but no frontend series was returned by any executed query (the frontend-filtered query returned only checkout and payment series), so frontend's own error and latency state was not observed and is unknown, not healthy.

Payment may be the origin of the errors checkout records, since a payment STATUS_CODE_ERROR series is present with higher counts (9-21) than checkout's (6-14). This is correlation only: no span was retrievable, so no checkout-to-payment parent-child edge, payment operation name or grpc status was observed, and a failing dependency would not by itself show which callers broke.

The checkout errors could alternatively arise inside checkout itself on specific operations (for example its own payment-client span or a handler), but this cannot be tested: span_name label values for checkout returned no_data and no error span, error detail or parent reference was available from Jaeger.

gaps: Jaeger traces are unavailable in this Run: four traces_search attempts (checkout over 2h, checkout over 1h, checkout with the default window, frontend over 30m) all returned status error with reason SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span, operation name, error detail field or parent-child call edge was observed for any service.
span_name label values for {__name__="traces_span_metrics_calls_total",service_name="checkout"} returned status no_data, so the operations behind checkout's error spans are unknown.

No Kubernetes state evidence exists: kubernetes_state is listed as not_integrated and the {__name__=~"kube_.*"} discovery returned only the two trace metric names, so no Deployment/ReplicaSet/Pod, image digest, readiness or restart evidence can place the fault on a Kubernetes object.
pod_logs and change_history are not integrated, so no deployment/configuration change in the window can be confirmed or excluded.

The metrics backend in this target appears to answer every expression with the same small series set (identical values for 5m, 10m and 1h ranges, filter-insensitive, and label-mismatched results for rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count and the duration bucket), so the returned values cannot be treated as reliable per-metric, per-operation readings and no trustworthy error ratio per operation or RPC exists.

The authorized window is a 24h historical window (2026-11-15T22:14:08 to 2026-11-16T22:14:08) and no samples outside it are readable, so there is no pre-window baseline against which to judge whether checkout's error counts are elevated versus normal.
No alert metadata (alert rule, threshold, start time) was supplied, so the instant the alerting signal began to deviate could not be determined from the evidence.
next_steps: Restore or verify Jaeger availability for m0-otel-20260909 and re-run traces_search for checkout and payment to obtain error spans, operation names, error detail text and parent references.

Inspect the checkout service's outgoing payment call (operation names, grpc status codes) once span data or a functioning rpc_client_duration_milliseconds series is available, to test the payment-origin hypothesis.
Add kube-state-metrics and change history for the otel-demo namespace so a Deployment/ReplicaSet change or pod restart coincident with the error signal can be checked.

Validate the Prometheus scrape/query path for this target, since metric responses ignored metric name, label and filter (rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count and duration buckets returned status_code-labelled series identical to traces_span_metrics_calls_total).
Obtain a baseline period (e.g. 24-48h before 2026-11-15T22:14:08) and the alert rule definition to establish when checkout's error rate actually deviated.
